blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the next four terms of the sequence: \(12, 16, 20, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
We are given the first three terms and must continue the list.
Plan: find the change from one term to the next; if it is always the same, keep applying it four more times.
steps:
Given: the terms \(12, 16, 20, \ldots\)
To find: the next four terms (4th to 7th).
Method: Find the difference between consecutive terms. The terms go up, so we expect the same change each time.

Find the change between consecutive terms
\[16 - 12 = 4\]
\[20 - 16 = 4\]
Why: Both differences are \(4\), so each term is the previous term plus \(4\).

Apply the rule four more times
\[a_4 = 20 + 4 = 24\]
\[a_5 = 24 + 4 = 28\]
\[a_6 = 28 + 4 = 32\]
\[a_7 = 32 + 4 = 36\]
Why: We start from the last given term and apply the same change for each new term.

Check
\[\text{gaps} = 4,\ 4,\ 4,\ 4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Every gap in the extended list is the same, so the pattern has been kept.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the next four terms of the sequence: \(3, 1, -1, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
We are given the first three terms and must continue the list.
Plan: find the change from one term to the next; if it is always the same, keep applying it four more times.
steps:
Given: the terms \(3, 1, -1, \ldots\)
To find: the next four terms (4th to 7th).
Method: Find the difference between consecutive terms. The terms go down, so we expect the same change each time.

Find the change between consecutive terms
\[1 - 3 = -2\]
\[-1 - 1 = -2\]
Why: Both differences are \(-2\), so each term is the previous term minus \(2\).

Apply the rule four more times
\[a_4 = -1 - 2 = -3\]
\[a_5 = -3 - 2 = -5\]
\[a_6 = -5 - 2 = -7\]
\[a_7 = -7 - 2 = -9\]
Why: We start from the last given term and apply the same change for each new term.

Check
\[\text{gaps} = -2,\ -2,\ -2,\ -2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Every gap in the extended list is the same, so the pattern has been kept.
